turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in. What has you here?
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long has the tiredness been at you?
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Give me a rough number if you can.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Six months. Is it a washed-out feeling?
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cold even with the heating going?
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm thinking aloud. Tired and perished for half a year makes me wonder about an underactive thyroid, but we'll park that. Weight?
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): A stone in that time. Eating more?
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): What do you blame it on?
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Night shifts would wreck you alright. Any constipation?
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain, or short of breath?
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is the mood low, or is it only the energy?
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke at all?
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Listen, the rain on the quays this morning was desperate. Did you get caught in it?
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): I was stuck twenty minutes at the lights by the church, hurling on the radio, Kilkenny, and I missed the second half completely.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Kilkenny, by two points. My brother-in-law had a tenner on them. He'll be unbearable.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): They say gales again at the weekend. My lot want Nowlan Park if it stays dry, which it won't. I'm rambling, ignore me.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Back to the bowels. You said no constipation. Is that the truth of it?
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): For how long, and how often are you going?
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the mood, you said it was only energy. Any flatness, feeling down?
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, so flat for those six months too. Thyroid problems in the family?
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): And were you tested, a thyroid blood test, any time?
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): What did they tell you?
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): Don't know. Actually, no. Cholesterol was borderline. Thyroid was grand, I think.
[SEG0065] person_1 (DOCTOR): So you're not certain, and I can't see an old result on the screen. Tablets now. Cholesterol?
[SEG0066] person_2 (PATIENT): Lipitor, twenty milligrams, mostly at night.
[SEG0067] person_1 (DOCTOR): So you miss the odd night?
[SEG0069] person_1 (DOCTOR): A water tablet, or inhalers?
[SEG0070] person_2 (PATIENT): Water tablet stopped in March. The purple inhaler, once, last winter.
[SEG0073] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me look at you. Hands are cold and a bit dry. Pulse is fifty-eight and regular. No swelling in the neck, and the ankles are grand.

[SEG0075] person_1 (DOCTOR): My working impression is an underactive thyroid. The cold, the tiredness, the stone of weight, the bowels, the flat mood, and your mam's history all point that way. I won't start a thyroid tablet until the bloods are back.
[SEG0077] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll send you for thyroid bloods, TSH and free T4, and a cholesterol check while we're at it.
[SEG0079] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back in a fortnight for the results. Keep on the Lipitor, leave that water tablet off, and ring the surgery if you're much worse before then.

spec.situation: Middle-aged person tired and cold for months, weight up, constipated, low mood; pins it on work and age; mother had thyroid disease; one old thyroid test result recalled wrongly ('borderline, they said'). Blood test planned.
features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Possible previous thyroid test mentioned, but patient is uncertain it happened.
Transcript uncertainty becomes whether thyroid test happened, not just when it was done.
bad.text: The patient cannot say when the previous thyroid blood test was done. (type=date_uncertain, related_entities=procedures_and_investigations[2], resolution_status=unresolved)
